Class MKScreen

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.AbstractContainerEventHandler
net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.screen.MKScreen
All Implemented Interfaces:
net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.ContainerEventHandler, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.GuiEventListener, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.Renderable, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.TabOrderedElement
public class MKScreen extends net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen
Base class for standalone screens built with MenuKit — full-screen, client-local, interactive UIs that are not tied to a container menu.

Extends vanilla's Screen directly; a MenuKit standalone screen is a vanilla Screen. Ecosystem mixins into Screen affect MenuKit standalone screens identically (vanilla-screen substitutability).

Holds a list of Panels (element-only; no slot groups — those are inventory-menu machinery). Layout is resolved via PanelLayout using the same PanelPosition constraint system inventory-menu screens use. Panels are centered on the screen; elements render on top of their panels; input is dispatched to elements in reverse panel order (top-most first) with the first consumer winning.

This is a minimal base class. Keyboard handling, focus management, and drag modes are not implemented — they'll land in later phases as the element palette surfaces need for them. See MKCHandledScreen inventory-menu analogue (holds slots + sync)

  • Field Details

    • PANEL_PADDING

      protected static final int PANEL_PADDING
      Padding inside each styled panel (pixels from panel edge to content). Phase 18r — actual padding applied is style-conditional via Panel.interiorPadding(): PANEL_PADDING for styled panels (RAISED / DARK / INSET), 0 for PanelStyle.NONE. The constant is retained for consumers who want the styled-panel value.

  • Method Details

    • setReturnAction

      protected void setReturnAction(@Nullable Runnable returnAction)
      Sets the action run when this screen closes via Escape (see returnAction). Subclasses also call runReturnAction() from their own "Back" chrome so Back and Escape agree. A null action (the default) leaves vanilla close behavior untouched.

    • hasReturnAction

      protected boolean hasReturnAction()
      Whether a return action is set (Back chrome can branch on this).

    • runReturnAction

      protected boolean runReturnAction()
      Runs the return action if one is set and returns true; otherwise returns false so the caller can fall back to its default navigation. Idempotent intent: the action is expected to setScreen(...) away from here.
